subQuestions.questionText: Product promotion using mass media involves …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Radio and television stations are forms of mass media used for product promotion.

subQuestions.questionText: The statement indicates the relationship between the price, supply and demand:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
As the price rises, the supply increases (producers want to sell more) and the demand decreases (consumers want to buy less).

options.A: The higher the price, the higher the demand and the lower the supply.
options.B: As the price rises, the supply increases and the demand decreases.
options.C: There is an inverse relationship between price, supply and demand.
options.D: As the price increases, the supply and demand decrease.

subQuestions.questionText: ONE of the following does NOT address an advantage of a free marketing system for farmers:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Lower marketing costs per unit is not an advantage of free marketing - in free marketing, individual farmers often have higher marketing costs per unit.

options.A: Selling where they want and at their own prices
options.C: Are encouraged to work hard and produce high quality products
options.D: Very little or no delay in receiving payment

subQuestions.questionText:
The following are TRUE about the standard format and components of an agribusiness plan:
(i) A standard business plan will include employees' personal details
(ii) Title page with business name, owner's details and address
(iii) Provides information on how the product is produced
(iv) Consists of marketing plan with target market
Choose the CORRECT combination below:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
(ii), (iii) and (iv) are true. A standard business plan does NOT include employees' personal details.

subQuestions.questionText: … does NOT imply restoration of land potential.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Practising overgrazing damages land - it does not restore land potential.

subQuestions.questionText: A farm worker who receives wages and benefits monthly until retirement:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
A permanent worker receives wages and benefits monthly until retirement.

subQuestions.questionText: Knowledge of veld management by a cattle production unit manager is aligned to the … skill.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Production and operational skill aligns with the practical knowledge of veld management.

subQuestions.questionText:
The following are the components of a Cash Flow Statement in a business:
(i) Receipts of operating income and capital sales
(ii) The value of assets and liabilities
(iii) Payments made for operating costs and expenses
(iv) The amount of cash available at the start of each month
Choose the CORRECT combination below:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
(i), (iii) and (iv) - The value of assets and liabilities (ii) belongs to a balance sheet, not a cash flow statement.

subQuestions.questionText: A pattern of inheritance shown by the alleles $I^A$, $I^B$ and $I^O$ determining the blood group is an example of ...
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Multiple alleles - blood group is determined by three alleles ($I^A$, $I^B$, $I^O$) at the same locus.

subQuestions.questionText: ONE of the following is NOT a technique used to genetically modify plants and animals:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Microporation is not a recognised technique for genetic modification. Electroporation, gene splicing and micro-injection are all valid techniques.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a term/phrase from COLUMN B that matches: The type of buyers who work for commission on behalf of other participants.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - brokers (2 marks)
Brokers work for commission on behalf of other market participants.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a term/phrase from COLUMN B that matches: The pathway that agricultural products take from farms to consumers.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: J - marketing chain (2 marks)
The marketing chain is the pathway that agricultural products take from farms to consumers.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a term/phrase from COLUMN B that matches: Responsible for putting strategies in place to keep a farm more productive and profitable.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - manager (2 marks)
A manager is responsible for putting strategies in place to keep a farm productive and profitable.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a term/phrase from COLUMN B that matches: Promotes economic development, social justice and democracy on the farm.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: E - Labour Relations Act, 1995 (Act 66 of 1995) (2 marks)
The Labour Relations Act promotes economic development, social justice and democracy in the workplace.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a term/phrase from COLUMN B that matches: Mutagenic agent caused by viruses.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - biological (2 marks)
Viruses are biological mutagenic agents that cause mutations.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: A measure of how the production and the provision of goods respond to a change in price.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Price elasticity of supply (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: An item with value that serves as security for credit.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Land (2 marks)
Land is commonly used as collateral/security for credit.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: A method of selecting animals that is based on the performance of the offspring.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Progeny selection (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: The total number of gene effects that are inherited and measured by the performance of the progeny.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Breeding value / BV (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: The use of statistics to analyse biological data.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Biometrics (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD to make TRUE: Shortage occurs when quantities of products supplied, exceed quantities demanded.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Surplus / over supply (1 mark)
A surplus (not shortage) occurs when supply exceeds demand.

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD to make TRUE: A budget is a legally binding document between a farmer and a farm worker.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Contract (1 mark)
A contract (not a budget) is a legally binding document between a farmer and farm worker.

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD to make TRUE: High heritability is determined mostly by environmental factors.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Genetic / internal (1 mark)
High heritability is determined mostly by genetic (internal) factors, not environmental factors.

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD to make TRUE: The repeated mating of unrelated superior bulls with inferior cows, generation after generation, refers to inbreeding.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Upgrading (1 mark)
Upgrading (not inbreeding) is the repeated mating of unrelated superior bulls with inferior cows.

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD to make TRUE: A pattern of inheritance where the offspring has an intermediate characteristic of the parents is complete dominance.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Incomplete (1 mark)
Incomplete dominance (not complete dominance) is when offspring has intermediate characteristics of the parents.

subQuestions.questionText: The diagram indicates the marketing functions: A (Products are changed into consumable commodities), B (Keeping products until they are needed), C (Enclosing products for distribution). Identify the marketing functions represented in A and B.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answers (2 marks - 1 mark each):
A - Storage
B - Packaging

Note: Based on the memo, A is identified as Storage and B as Packaging (the descriptions in the diagram appear to be presented in a different order to the labels).

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO advantages of the marketing function represented in C (processing - products are changed into consumable commodities).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 of the following (2 marks):
• Reduces wastage of excess produce
• Provides job opportunities
• Increases the value of the product
• Allows easier packaging/handling/transportation of products
• It is a way of overcoming over-supply of products
• Increases the shelf-life of a product/prevents spoilage
• Improves food safety
• The product is available throughout the year
• It is a way for farmers to increase their share of the final price for a product
• Products are more convenient for the consumer

subQuestions.questionText: Name the marketing function that is NOT indicated above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Transportation (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the statement applies to marketing or selling: It occurs when decisions are made before the manufacturing cycle of the products to be produced.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Marketing (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the statement applies to marketing or selling: It offers the products that are already produced.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Selling (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the statement applies to marketing or selling: It involves the designing of the product so that it becomes acceptable to consumers.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Marketing (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: The diagram illustrates the supply and demand in a market (showing 250 bags of supply at R25/bag balanced with 250 bags of demand at R25/bag, with Price as the fulcrum). Name the condition in the market that is illustrated by the diagram above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Market equilibrium / equilibrium price (1 mark)
This condition occurs when supply equals demand at a particular price.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate what will happen to the price of a product when supply is more than demand.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (1 mark):
The price of a product will be low / less.

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO factors that determine the supply of a product.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 of the following (2 marks):
• Price of a product
• Production costs
• Technology
• Nature/environment/season
• Government subsidies
• Number of suppliers/producers
• Price expectation
• Research
• Legislation
• Political developments
• Demand for the product
• Competitive products
• Possibility of increasing the supply of products

subQuestions.questionText: The diagram illustrates the marketing approach commonly used by farmers in a market (showing potatoes being marketed via Internet, Retailers/Supermarket, and Processing factories - one product to multiple channels/segments). Identify the marketing approach illustrated in the diagram above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Mass marketing (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 2.4.1 above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 of the following (1 mark):
• The larger/whole market is targeted with a single offer
• Promotes the same product in different ways to different groups of consumers

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO other marketing approaches that are used to market agricultural products.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 of the following (2 marks):
• Niche marketing
• Multi-segment marketing
• Sustainable marketing

subQuestions.questionText: The picture illustrates farmers working together to pool their products for sale (showing many hands joined together with 'TEAMWORK' theme). Deduce the marketing system represented in the picture above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Cooperative marketing (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE type of the marketing system in QUESTION 2.5.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 of the following (1 mark):
• Production
• Processing
• Marketing
• Agricultural inputs and service / commercial
• Purchasing
• Consumer

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO principles of the marketing system represented in the picture above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 of the following (2 marks):
• Voluntary and open membership
• Members contribute equally / members economic participation
• Each member has a single vote
• Democratic in nature
• Autonomy and independence
• Based on pool system
• Cooperation amongst members/cooperatives
• Assists in training and educating its members
• Members receive a limited interest on their share capital
• Only members may deliver products and benefit
• Products from members are standardised before selling
• Products are graded according to quality and members paid in advance
• After liquidation surplus is shared amongst members
• Concern for the community

subQuestions.questionText:
The pictures represent different marketing channels used by farmers. PICTURE A: Produce sold at the farm entrance. PICTURE B: Marketing of produce online. PICTURE C: Livestock sold to the highest bidder. Identify the marketing channels represented in:
(a) PICTURE B
(b) PICTURE C
subQuestions.memoText:
Answers (2 marks - 1 mark each):
(a) PICTURE B - Internet / online marketing
(b) PICTURE C - Stock sales / auction

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO advantages of the marketing channel represented in PICTURE A (Produce sold at the farm entrance / farm gate marketing) for the consumer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Both of the following (2 marks - 1 mark each):
• Consumers get products at a cheaper price / low price
• Fresh / quality products for the consumer

subQuestions.questionText: Match the statement with the factor that hampers the marketing of agricultural products (A: PERISHABILITY, B: POOR INFRASTRUCTURE, C: LONG DISTANCES TO MARKETS): Producing closer to markets.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Long distance to markets / C (1 mark)
Producing closer to markets is a solution to the problem of long distances to markets.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the statement with the factor that hampers the marketing of agricultural products: Provision of cooler trucks or containers to prevent spoilage during transportation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Perishability / A (1 mark)
Cooler trucks/containers prevent spoilage of perishable products.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the statement with the factor that hampers the marketing of agricultural products: Improving the condition of roads in rural areas to facilitate marketing.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Poor infrastructure / B (1 mark)
Improving roads addresses the problem of poor infrastructure.

subQuestions.questionText:
The flow diagram illustrates the phases of the entrepreneurial process: Phase 1 (unknown), Phase 2 (Developing a business plan), Phase 3 (unknown), Phase 4 (Starting a business and managing it). State the phases of the entrepreneurial process represented by:
(a) 1
(b) 3
subQuestions.memoText:
Answers (2 marks - 1 mark each):
(a) 1 - Identification of a business opportunity
(b) 3 - Determining the resources required / resource mobilization

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons for having phase 2 (Developing a business plan) in the entrepreneurial process.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 of the following (2 marks):
• Documenting the business idea
• Test the feasibility and economic viability of a business
• Determine the financial needs of the business
• Secure funding for the business
• Ensure effective business management
• Allow the farmer to foresee problems
• Gain knowledge about marketing opportunities/competitors
• Reposition the business to deal with changes in the market
• Guide daily operations
• Set a goal/vision for the business

subQuestions.questionText: The diagram explains the components of the SWOT analysis. A: Competitors closeby have a similar product to that of the farmer. B: Products from competitors are expensive and not available at all times. C: Good relations with customers resulting from good marketing strategies. D: The farm is struggling to meet targets due to cash flow problems. Identify the letter (A–D) that represents Opportunity.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: B (1 mark)
Products from competitors being expensive and not available at all times represents an Opportunity (external positive factor).

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the letter (A–D) that represents Weakness.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: D (1 mark)
The farm struggling to meet targets due to cash flow problems represents a Weakness (internal negative factor).

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the letter (A–D) that represents Threat.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: A (1 mark)
Competitors closeby having a similar product represents a Threat (external negative factor).

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the letter (A–D) that represents Strength.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: C (1 mark)
Good relations with customers resulting from good marketing strategies represents a Strength (internal positive factor).

subQuestions.questionText: The picture shows sheep raised on a piece of land (showing sheep grazing). State TWO functions of land as depicted in the picture above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Both of the following (2 marks - 1 mark each):
• Land provides space
• Land provides food

subQuestions.questionText: State THREE economic characteristics of land.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 3 of the following (3 marks):
• Land is subject to the law of diminishing returns
• Agricultural land is limited
• Land cannot be destroyed / indestructible
• Land differs with regard to production potential
• Land is durable
• Land can serve as collateral
• Land can be bought or sold
• Value of the land varies
• The value of land appreciates
• Land is found in a specific environment / fixed
• Primary factor for production
• Passive factor for production

subQuestions.questionText: Labour is a huge expenditure in a farming enterprise. State TWO components of a contract between a farmer and a farm worker.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 of the following (2 marks):
• Employer and employee details
• Job title, job description and place of work
• Renumeration / wages
• Notice period and termination of employment / period of employment
• Allowances / incentives
• Hours of work and meal intervals
• Deductions from salary
• Payment of overtime and over the holidays
• Leave and other benefits
• Signatures of employer and employee
• Date of payment

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate TWO labour problems resulting from farm workers moving to other industries.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 of the following (2 marks):
• Poor working conditions
• Poor living conditions
• Long working hours / overtime
• Exposure to harsh weather conditions
• Lack of career opportunities / promotion
• Economic migration / low wages / no payment for public holidays
• Social problems
• Competition from other industries
• Lack of training opportunities

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest TWO ways in which a farmer can retain farm workers.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 of the following (2 marks):
• Better working conditions
• Better living conditions
• Reasonable working hours
• Replacement of the hard manual labour with machinery / efficient mechanisation
• Provide education / training / skills development / empowerment
• Better wages / bonuses
• Entering into partnerships with workers
• Incentives / supply workers with farm products

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate the implication of EACH of the following labour Acts on the working conditions of farm workers:
(a) Basic Conditions of Employment Act, 1997 (Act 95 of 1997)
(b) Occupational Health and Safety Act, 1993 (Act 85 of 1993)
subQuestions.memoText:
Answers (2 marks - 1 mark each):
(a) Basic Conditions of Employment Act, 1997 (Act 95 of 1997):
Regulates leave / working hours / employment contracts / deductions / wages / termination of employment

(b) Occupational Health and Safety Act, 1993 (Act 85 of 1993) - Any 1:
• Ensuring the safety of workers in the workplace
• Enforces proper training when operating machinery / equipment / tools
• Ensures the provision of protective gear / equipment
• Provides guidelines on safe working environment

subQuestions.questionText:
The schematic representation shows different capital items found on a farm: A (Land, buildings and fences), B (Seeds, feed and fuel), C (Livestock, tractors and machinery). Indicate the type of capital represented by EACH of the following:
(a) B
(b) C
(c) A
subQuestions.memoText:
Answers (3 marks - 1 mark each):
(a) B - Working / floating / production capital
(b) C - Movable capital
(c) A - Fixed capital

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest TWO methods of creating capital in a farming business.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 of the following (2 marks):
• Production
• Savings / own capital / investments
• Credit / loans
• Inheritance / family
• Business partners
• Grant / donations
• Trust companies

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify the problem of capital the farmer is likely to encounter with regard to EACH of the following statements:
(a) Aging, wear and tear of farm machinery and vehicles
(b) Inability to acquire capital items such as machinery, land, buildings and livestock
(c) Theft, occurrence of diseases among livestock, incidences of droughts and pests
subQuestions.memoText:
Answers (3 marks - 1 mark each):
(a) Depreciation
(b) Scarcity of capital / expensive capital / high interest
(c) Risk

subQuestions.questionText: The table shows the assets and liabilities of a farming business. ASSETS: Current assets R205 000, Medium-term assets R1 050 000, Long-term assets R3 500 000, TOTAL ASSETS A. LIABILITIES: Current liabilities R75 000, Medium-term liabilities R150 000, Long-term liabilities R1 000 000, TOTAL LIABILITIES B. Identify the type of financial record represented in the table above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Balance sheet (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Determine the value of EACH of the following:
(a) A (Total Assets)
(b) B (Total Liabilities)
Name the document used to record all the farm assets.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Inventory (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the net worth using the data in the table above. Show ALL calculations including the formula.
subQuestions.memoText:
Marks (3 marks - 1 mark each):
Mark 1: Formula: $\text{Net worth} = \text{Total assets} - \text{Total liabilities}$
Mark 2: $= R4\,755\,000 - R1\,225\,000$
Mark 3: $= R3\,530\,000$

subQuestions.questionText: A group of farmers started farming with different crops and citrus fruits. They began experiencing a drop in citrus production due to insect infestations. They had to substitute citrus with avocado and banana plants. Identify TWO risk management strategies that will benefit the farmers in the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Both of the following (2 marks - 1 mark each):
• Diversification
• Risk-sharing

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for EACH risk management strategy identified in QUESTION 3.5.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Both of the following (2 marks - 1 mark each):
• Diversification - There are different crops/enterprises on the farm
• Risk-sharing - Farmers are working as a group

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the primary source of risk in the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Technical / production risk (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the type of force that influences the farming business represented by: Money available to spend by consumers.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: External (1 mark)
Consumer spending power is an external factor that influences the farming business.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the type of force that influences the farming business represented by: Equipment and workforce available on a farm.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Internal (1 mark)
Equipment and workforce on a farm are internal factors.

subQuestions.questionText: The genotypes of individuals differ from one animal to the other, giving rise to different phenotypes among animals within the same species. Differentiate between genotype and phenotype.
subQuestions.memoText:
Both of the following (2 marks - 1 mark each):
• Genotype - Genetic make-up of an organism
• Phenotype - Physical characteristic of an organism

subQuestions.questionText: Name the phenomenon that refers to the differences in phenotypes among animals of the same species.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Variation (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO factors that can cause the phenomenon named in QUESTION 4.1.2 above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 of the following (2 marks):
• Internal / genetic factors
• Meiosis
• Crossing over
• Random arrangement of chromosomes
• Random fertilization
• Mutation
• External / environmental factors
• Diseases
• Feeding / nutrition
• Topography
• Climate

subQuestions.questionText: The pedigree diagram shows the inheritance of colour from the crossing of a red rooster and a pure-bred white hen. (Generation 1: individuals 1 and 2; Generation 2: individuals 3, 4, 5, 6; Generation 3: individuals 7, 8, 9. Shaded = Red, Unshaded = White, ◯ = Female, □ = Male.) Determine the number of generations in the pedigree diagram above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Three (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the process that occurred between the gametes of individuals 1 and 2 that resulted in individuals with numbers 3, 4 and 5 in the crossing above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Fertilization (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the phenotype of individual 8.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: White (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether individual 1 is homozygous or heterozygous.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Heterozygous (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Justify, with a reason, the answer to QUESTION 4.2.4 above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (1 mark):
Produced offspring number 3 which is white homozygous recessive (showing that individual 1 must carry the recessive white allele).

subQuestions.questionText: A heterozygous black (B) goat with floppy ears (s) is crossed with a white (b) goat with heterozygous sharp (S) ears. The colour black is dominant over white, and sharp ears are dominant over floppy ears. (Punnett square shown with gametes Bs, bs, Bs, bs across the top and bS, bs, bS, bs down the side, with offspring genotypes filled in.) Identify the type of crossing represented in the Punnett square above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Dihybrid (cross) (1 mark)
A dihybrid cross involves two pairs of contrasting characteristics (colour and ear type).

subQuestions.questionText: Name the genotype of the parent with floppy ears.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Bbss (1 mark)
The parent with floppy ears is heterozygous black (Bb) with homozygous recessive floppy ears (ss).

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate the phenotype of EACH of the following individuals:
(a) Number 1
(b) Number 2
subQuestions.memoText:
Answers (2 marks - 1 mark each):
(a) Number 1 (bbSs) - White with sharp ears
(b) Number 2 (Bbss) - Black with floppy ears

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the percentage of individuals that are genotypically the same as the white parent.
subQuestions.memoText:
Marks (2 marks - 1 mark each):
Mark 1: $\frac{4}{16} \times 100$
Mark 2: $= 25\%$

(The white parent has genotype bbSs; 4 out of 16 offspring in the Punnett square share this genotype.)

subQuestions.questionText: Height in animals is one of the traits that is considered for breeding. Assuming that the height in cattle is influenced by three pairs of genes, with a base height (aabbdd) of 135 cm, each additive allele contributes 10 cm to the base height. Calculate the height of the animal with an AaBbDD genotype.
subQuestions.memoText:
Marks (2 marks - 1 mark each):
Mark 1: $= 135 \text{ cm} + (4 \times 10 \text{ cm})$
Mark 2: $= 175 \text{ cm}$

(AaBbDD has 4 additive (capital letter) alleles: A, B, D, D)

subQuestions.questionText: Determine ONE genotype of an animal with a height of 185 cm.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 of the following (1 mark):
• AaBBDD
• AABbDD
• AABBDd

(Height = 185 cm requires $185 - 135 = 50$ cm above base, which means 5 additive alleles.)

subQuestions.questionText: The graph represents a normal distribution curve used in the selection of cows for a breeding programme based on their milk production (showing Group A in poor performance area, Group B in average performance area, and Group C in excellent performance area). Identify in the graph above the most suitable group of animals (A, B or C) to be selected as parents in a breeding programme for the next generation.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Group C (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 4.5.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 of the following (1 mark):
• Select animals that perform above the average of the herd
• The performance of these animals is superior to animals in Group A and B

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the method of selection used in the breeding programme above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Mass selection (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The letters (A–D) represent breeding systems commonly used by farmers:
A - Brahman bull X daughter
B - Nguni bull X Sussex cows
C - Different superior Bonsmara bulls X inferior cows generation after generation
D - Male donkey X female horse
Identify the breeding system that produces maximum hybrid vigour.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: B (1 mark)
Nguni bull X Sussex cows (crossbreeding two different breeds) produces maximum hybrid vigour.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the breeding system (A–D) where the offspring are hardy and can work under unfavourable conditions.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: D (1 mark)
Male donkey X female horse produces a mule, which is hardy and can work under unfavourable conditions (out-crossing/hybridization between species).

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the breeding system (A–D) that leads to deformities.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: A (1 mark)
Brahman bull X daughter (inbreeding - mating closely related individuals) leads to deformities.

subQuestions.questionText:
The table shows the heritability of different characteristics in cattle and goat breeds:
Birth-weight: Cattle 38%, Goats 35%
Post-wean weight: Cattle 30%, Goats 60%
Meat tenderness: Cattle 65%, Goats 35%
Lean meat: Cattle 38%, Goats 90%
Slaughter weight: Cattle 90%, Goats 65%
Draw a line graph to compare the heritability of different characteristics in cattle and goat breeds.
subQuestions.memoText:
Marking criteria (6 marks - 1 mark each):
• Correct heading with both variables - e.g. 'Heritability of cattle and goats for different characteristics'
• X-axis: Correctly calibrated and labelled (Characteristics)
• Y-axis: Correctly calibrated and labelled (Heritability)
• Correct units (%)
• Line graph (two lines - one for cattle, one for goats, with a key/legend)
• Accuracy (80% + correctly plotted)

subQuestions.questionText: Genetic modification is a technique used to alter the genetic composition of organisms. State TWO potential benefits of GM crops for the environment.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 of the following (2 marks):
• Farmers use less pesticides
• Allow for no-tillage farming
• Environment assessment is carried out for all GM crops

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO advantages of genetic modification over traditional methods.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 of the following (2 marks):
• It is precise
• It is fast
• Not limited to organisms of the same species
